incoming.explanation: The open Warford identity is raised by, and turns on, the 1627 letter.

outgoing.explanation: The 1627 letter documents the senior branch's Court-of-Wards channel to Winthrop and Downing on which the finding rests.

shortLabel: 1627 Gurdon–Winthrop letter: 'mrs. Gurny' presents through the Court of Wards

sources.alignmentNote: Names Winthrop at the Court of Wards, Emmanuel Downing, the widow-guardian 'mrs. Gurny,' and her nearly-of-age heir 'yong mr. gurney.'
sources.excerpt: he hathe a presentatyon from mrs. Gurny who is gardyon to her sonn who wantethe a few monthes of being of ful age ... yong mr. gurney commethe with him
sources.locator: Winthrop Papers, vol. I (1929), p. 363; MHS Winthrop Family Papers Digital Edition, PWF01d256

statement: Brampton Gurdon of Assington's letter to John Winthrop, 20 October 1627, asks Winthrop — then an attorney at the Court of Wards and Liveries — to further a clergyman's suit to the Master of the Wards over a church presentation held by 'mrs. Gurny who is gardyon to her sonn who wantethe a few monthes of being of ful age,' whom 'yong mr. gurney' attends, with commendations to Emmanuel Downing. It is the only Gurney-variant document in the whole Winthrop Family Papers.
